div.head: Af El. 12
div.ab: Ðeah hwa gebycgge his dohtor on þeowenne, ne sie hio ealles swa ðeowu swa oðru mennenu: nage he hie ut on elðeodig folc to bebycgganne. Ac gif he hire ne recce, se ðe hie bohte, læte hie freo on elðeodig folc. Gif he ðonne alefe his suna mid to hæmanne, do hiere gyfta: locige þæt hio hæbbe hrægl; ⁊ þæt weorð sie hiere mægðhades, þæt is se weotuma, agife he hire þone. Gif he hire þara nan ne do, þonne sie hio frioh.

Though someone should buy his [the Christian slave’s] daughter in servitude, let her not be entirely as much a slave as other maidservants: he has not the power to sell her to a strange people. But if he does not like her, whom he bought, he shall let her go free among a strange folk. However, if he allows his son to have her, let him [the son] give her [marriage-] gifts: let him look that she have clothing; and the worth of her maidenhood, that is the bride-price, let him give her that. If he does none of these things for her, then let her be free.

Ðeah hwa gebicge his dohter to þeowte, ne beo heo alles swa þeow swa oðer þeowwifman: nage he hy utt on ælþeodig folc to syllanne. Ac gif he hyre ne recce, se þe hy bohte, læte hy frige on ælþeodig folc. Gif he þonne alyfe hys sune mid to hæmenne, do hyre gifta 7 locie þæt heo hæbbe hrægl; 7 þæt sy wurð hire mægþhades, þæt his se wítuma, agyfe hire þene. Gif he hyre þare nanne ne dó, þonne sy heo freoh.
